title: Colombian Waitresses y Jueces canadienses: Gender and Country Biases in Occupation Recommendations from LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting large language models for occupation recommendations while systematically varying the subject's pronouns (including masculine, feminine, and non-binary/neo-pronouns) across English, Spanish, and German, then clustering the generated jobs and measuring distributional inequality using L2 norm and Jensen-Shannon divergence.

Prompting large language models for occupation recommendations using templates that vary the subject's country of origin (using 25 distinct countries), and evaluating how the distribution of suggested job clusters changes based on the specified country.

Evaluating the compounded, intersecting effects of bias by simultaneously varying both the gender proxy (pronouns) and the country of origin in the job recommendation prompts to identify harms masked by single-axis evaluations.
